title: Org-scoped probe suites with client-side no-telemetry mode
creator: Leah Chen
description: Problem: Customers running Dedicated or Private deployments require regression monitoring tied to model/config changes but cannot send representative prompts or outputs to Redwood for privacy or compliance reasons. Goal: Ship an org-scoped evaluation runner and probe suite pattern that can be executed inside customer environments (VPC/on-prem) or as a suppressed-telemetry hosted run. Provide a client-side 'no-telemetry' mode that keeps raw prompts/outputs local, uploads only hashed anchors and aggregated metrics, and integrates with Redwood Console rollouts and alerting. Scope: 1) Define minimal on-prem eval manifest format (golden-set references, metrics, thresholds, trigger conditions). 2) Build a lightweight eval-runner binary (Go) that can be deployed as an init job or cron job in Private & Dedicated environments. 3) Add a privacy-preserving telemetry adapter that uploads HMAC anchors and differential counts instead of raw text. 4) Console UX: per-org eval dashboard, per-change gating (config/model) and canary gate integration. Trade-offs: - Local execution increases operational surface and customer onboarding work vs. best-accuracy goldens in-cloud. - HMAC-hashed anchors prevent us from reproducing outputs; will limit some root-cause diagnosis. - Rolling out a binary implies extra OS/package support and security review. Success metrics: - 30% of new Private/Dedicated customers opt into org-scoped evals within 90 days of private launch. - Detect regressions with >90% true-positive rate on seeded failures during internal tests. Deliverables: - Eval manifest spec (Confluence), 0.1 binary (Linux x86_64), Console gating flow, onboarding doc and security review. Acceptance criteria enumerated below.

acceptance_criteria: Spec: Eval manifest spec published and reviewed in Confluence with examples for regression, latency, and hallucination probes.
Runner: Linux x86_64 eval-runner v0.1 can execute a manifest against a pinned model/config and produce a metric bundle.
Privacy: Telemetry adapter can run in 'no-telemetry' mode (no outbound raw prompts/outputs) and in 'masked' mode (uploads only HMAC anchors and aggregated counts).
Console: Console can display per-org eval runs, historical trend, and surface gating status for a rollout tied to model/config change.
Security: Security review completed and binary signing + KMS/HSM integration documented with approval from Security team.
Onboarding: Customer-facing runbook and helm example present in the repo and Confluence.
